key_fields.sql: select z.borough, count(*) as touches from lake.trips t join ops.zones z on z.locationid = t.pulocationid or z.locationid = t.dolocationid group by z.borough order by z.borough
key_fields.claim: An OR inside the JOIN condition cannot use a hash join; the engine falls back to a nested-loop style join, which is far more expensive than two equi-joins. (matched: inner join ops.zones z on z.locationid = t.pulocationid or z.locationid = t.dolocationid)

value.sql: SELECT borough, SUM(touches) AS touches FROM (SELECT z.Borough AS borough, COUNT(*) AS touches FROM lake.trips t JOIN ops.zones z ON z.LocationID = t.PULocationID GROUP BY z.Borough UNION ALL SELECT z.Borough AS borough, COUNT(*) AS touches FROM lake.trips t JOIN ops.zones z ON z.LocationID = t.DOLocationID GROUP BY z.Borough) sub GROUP BY borough ORDER BY borough
value.change_summary: Split the OR join into two separate equi-joins (PU and DO), each aggregated per borough, then combined with UNION ALL and a final SUM aggregation to preserve exact per-borough counts.
value.risk_notes: Requires ops.zones.LocationID to be unique (it is: 265 distinct non-NULL values). If a trip row has identical PULocationID and DOLocationID, it will be counted twice, matching the original OR-join semantics.
